name: CASPEr
summary: An international program using nuclear spins to sense axion dark matter, with Electric and Gradient / Wind approaches.
detection_principle: Axion-induced oscillating electric dipole moments or spin-gradient coupling exert resonant torques on nuclear spins; nuclear magnetic resonance detects their precession.

status.label: Multiphase project: completed experiments alongside further construction / design
status.evidence: 2021 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Search for axion-like dark matter using solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance

collaboration.name: CASPEr Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

phases.name: CASPEr-Electric
phases.description: Uses internal electric fields to detect oscillating electric dipole moments.

phases.name: CASPEr-Gradient / Wind
phases.description: Uses the nuclear-spin response to dark-matter-field gradients.

results.summary: The solid-state NMR experiment found no signal and constrained axion electric-dipole and gradient couplings.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
